title: Public method is callable from the browser
msg: Any public method on a Livewire component can be called by the browser as $wire.NAME(). This file contains no authorize(), Gate::, can() or abort_unless() call, so NAME() runs for anyone who can open the page.
fix: Open the method with $this->authorize('update', $model) (or Gate::authorize), or mark the method protected if the view does not call it.

title: Public property is writable from the browser
msg: Livewire round-trips every public property through the page, so the browser can send back any value for $NAME before the next method runs.
fix: Add the #[Livewire\Attributes\Locked] attribute above the property, or re-read the value from the database instead of trusting the round-trip.

title: Secret held in a public property
msg: Public Livewire properties are serialized into the rendered HTML snapshot, so $NAME is readable in view-source by anyone who loads the page.
fix: Move the value to a protected property, to session, or read it from config() inside the method that needs it.

title: Unescaped Blade echo
msg: {!! !!} prints the value with no HTML escaping, so any markup or <script> stored in that value runs in the visitor's browser.
fix: Use {{ }} instead, or sanitize the value before printing it.

title: Template name comes from a variable
msg: @include/@component with a variable template name lets whatever fills that variable choose which view is rendered.
fix: Name the view literally, or map the variable through a fixed allow-list array before including it.

title: Query-string property feeds identity or state
msg: #[Url] binds this property to the query string, so the value of $NAME is set by whatever the visitor types into the address bar.
fix: Keep #[Url] for view state only. For an identifier, resolve the record through a policy or scope owned by the signed-in user.

title: Upload stored without validation
msg: This component uses WithFileUploads and stores the file, but the file has no validate() or #[Validate] rule anywhere in the class, so the type and size of what lands on disk are the visitor's choice.

title: mount() loads a record with no ownership check
msg: mount() receives its arguments from the page that renders the component and looks a record up, but the class has no authorize(), Gate::, can() or abort_unless() call, so any signed-in visitor can mount another tenant's record.
fix: Add $this->authorize('view', $record) in mount(), or scope the lookup to auth()->user().

title: Browser-held state written straight to the model
msg: This line writes component state the browser can rewrite into the database in one call, so every unlocked public property on this class becomes a writable database column.
fix: Write an explicit array of validated fields, e.g. $model->update($this->validate()), and lock the properties that must not change.

title: Debug dump left in a rendered component
msg: dd()/dump()/var_dump() prints the variable into the response, so whatever it holds is shown to whoever loads the page.
fix: Remove the call, or replace it with Log::debug().
